newsitem.title: ITALY: World Food Day paves the way to food summit.
newsitem.headline: World Food Day paves the way to food summit.

text.p: The United Nations staged events in many countries on Wednesday to mark its annual World Food Day and publicise a summit in Rome next month that will tackle ways of combatting hunger.
The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) says it expects around 100 heads of state and government to attend the last three days of the summit which runs from November 13 to 17.
A World Food Day ceremony at FAO's Rome headquarters on Wednesday included a speech by Ivory Coast President Henri Konan Bedie and a message from Pope John Paul.

FAO director-general Jacques Diouf said this year's World Food Day theme, "Fighting Hunger and Malnutrition," was chosen because of "the continuing logic-defying paradox of a planet that produces enough for everyone but at the same time has over 800 million people who have no guarantee of an adequate diet".
He said the summit would give world leaders the opportunity to publically state their commitment to fighting hunger and help "restore agriculture to its rightful priority status".
"Hunger only gives the world wasted resources, wasted human potential, social and political unrest, misery and death," Diouf said. "So we have no choice but to react.
Although Wednesday is the official World Food Day, marking the anniversary of the creation of FAO 51 years ago, related events were planned for the coming weeks.
It will be observed on October 25 at United Nations headquarters in New York, and FAO and the city of Rome have organised a World Food Day concert in front of the ancient Colosseum on October 27.

The FAO said events held in other parts of the world included mango tree plantings in the Maldives, the launch of a a campaign to "use grain economically" in Chinese provinces, cooking demonstrations in Benin, a German Internet presentation and the distribution of food baskets in rural areas of Grenada.

The Pope, in his message, also spoke of "the paradox" of the world food outlook. His message was written by Vatican Secretary of State, Cardinal Angelo Sodano, and read at the FAO ceremony by the Vatican's FAO representative, Cardinal Alois Wagner.

"While the goals which the human family has achieved encourage us to hope for a future ever more responsive to human needs, the world remains divided between those who live in abundance and those who lack the necessary daily bread," the Pope's message said.
Bedie, in his speech to FAO, highlighted the particular needs of Africa.
He said the lack of affordable irrigation systems was "the weakness of agricultural yield in Africa", adding: "Food security can only be mastered with water control".
